findings.body:
The test enforces an important invariant, but it does so by exposing `--expose-gc`, creating `WeakRef`s to internal chunks, and forcing collection between pulls. That is a side-channel/implementation-detail test: it will break if the reader is refactored to hold chunks legitimately while still discarding the entry logically (for example, to support backpressure or streaming checks). It also depends on Node/V8 GC behavior and could flake under different versions or flags.

A more robust test would assert the observable behavior: a too-large file is yielded with `body: undefined` and the reader returns the next file without requiring memory growth. If memory behavior must be pinned, document it as an explicit contract with a small helper comment that no earlier chunk should be retained (already in the title), and ideally guard the test so it is skipped when `--expose-gc` is unavailable or runs in CI.

One intended departure from issue #32 is noted in the description: prices come from pi-ai's registry rather than a hand-maintained price table in code. The issue says "Convert tokens to neurons and dollars from a per-model price table in code", so this changes the requested mechanism; it still meets the functional goal and is documented in `docs/design.md`.

However, the new `.filter(([count]) => count > 0)` drops zero-valued parts, so exact-hour and exact-minute durations render without their trailing zero units. findings.title: Zero unit parts are dropped, changing the rendered duration
findings.basis: Existing tests at `test/cost.test.ts:313-316` expect `durationText(3_600)` to render as `1h 0m 0s` and `durationText(120)` as `2m 0s`, preserving zero-valued units between non-zero higher units and the trailing seconds component.
findings.body:
This filter removes every unit whose count is zero, so `3600` becomes `1h` instead of `1h 0m 0s`, `120` becomes `2m` instead of `2m 0s`, and `3660` becomes `1h 1m` instead of `1h 1m 0s`. That contradicts the description’s claim of “No change in what the footer shows” and will fail the existing tests that document the intended format. Keep the first non-zero unit and every unit after it (including the final seconds) rather than dropping zeros unconditionally.

One way to preserve the one-list structure and the original output is to slice from the first non-zero part instead of filtering:
```typescript
function durationText(seconds: number): string {
  const parts = [
    [Math.floor(seconds / 3600), "h"],
    [Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60), "m"],
    [seconds % 60, "s"],
  ] as const
  const start = parts.findIndex(([count]) => count > 0)
  return parts
    .slice(start === -1 ? parts.length - 1 : start)
    .map(([count, unit]) => `${count}${unit}`)
    .join(" ")
}
```

findings.basis: The filter keeps only non-zero parts, but the old implementation kept zero-valued minutes when hours were present and always kept seconds; for 3,600 seconds the footer changes from "sandbox 1h 0m 0s" to "sandbox 1h", and for 120 seconds from "sandbox 2m 0s" to "sandbox 2m".
findings.body: The PR description states "No change in what the footer shows," yet this filter removes intermediate zero units that were previously rendered. The old code showed minutes whenever hours were present (`minutes > 0 || hours > 0`) and always showed seconds. The existing test at `test/cost.test.ts:314` encodes this expectation with `spendLine([spend({})], 3_600)` containing `" · sandbox 1h 0m 0s ($0.074)"` and `120` containing `" · sandbox 2m 0s ($0.002)"`. To build from one list while preserving the visual output, keep every part from the first non-zero unit onwards instead of dropping all zero counts.
findings.suggestion:
const parts = [
    [Math.floor(seconds / 3600), "h"],
    [Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60), "m"],
    [seconds % 60, "s"],
  ] as const
  const first = parts.findIndex(([count]) => count > 0)
  return parts
    .slice(first)
    .map(([count, unit]) => `${count}${unit}`)
    .join(" ")

submission.summary: This PR changes `checkTimeoutOf` in `src/sandbox/checks.ts` to return `undefined` for unset/unparsable `SANDBOX_CHECK_TIMEOUT` and updates the unit test to expect `undefined`. The intended outcome—"so the default lives with the caller"—is not realized because the only caller, `src/pull-request.ts:606`, still passes the result straight into `RunOptions.timeoutMs` without supplying a fallback. That leaves the default with neither the parser nor the caller, so sandbox checks time out immediately when the env var is missing or invalid.

findings.title: Doc line misstates pnpm argument forwarding
findings.basis: package.json declares `"deploy": "wrangler deploy"`; `pnpm run <script> -- <args>` forwards the args to that script, so the wrapped command becomes `wrangler deploy --var SANDBOX_PROBE:true` and `--var` is not dropped.
findings.body: The added sentence claims that `pnpm run deploy -- --var SANDBOX_PROBE:true` drops the `--var` argument, but pnpm's `run` command forwards arguments after the script name (and after `--`) to the script. With `package.json`'s `"deploy": "wrangler deploy"`, that command ultimately runs `wrangler deploy --var SANDBOX_PROBE:true`. If a specific pnpm or wrangler version in this repo actually drops the argument, document that exact scenario; otherwise this clause is misleading and should be removed or corrected.

findings.title: Removing trim breaks quote matching for indented lines
findings.body: A reviewer quoting an indented line such as `  return a + b;` without copying the leading spaces exactly will see the finding rejected. The callers in `src/review/findings.ts` (`anchorByQuote`, `relocateByQuote`) and `src/review/incremental.ts` compare `comparableText(quote)` with `comparableText(lineText)`. With `.trim()` removed, `"  return a + b;"` normalises to `" return a + b;"` while `"return a + b;"` stays `"return a + b;"`, so a quote that omits indentation no longer matches. This also affects `deltaLines`/`markedLines`: a line that is only re-indented will now be treated as changed, altering which lines are marked in incremental reviews. Preserve `.trim()` so whitespace at the edges stays irrelevant to matching.

accepted.basis: comparableText is used to compare diff-line content in findings.ts (anchorByQuote/relocateByQuote), incremental.ts (touchedByPush/movedFrom), and to detect moved lines in markedLines. Removing .trim() makes surrounding whitespace significant: a source line "foo  " normalizes to "foo " while the same line copied without trailing spaces normalizes to "foo", so a valid reviewer quote can fail validation and a moved/deleted line can be missed.
accepted.title: comparableText no longer strips surrounding whitespace
accepted.body: The function is meant to make diff-line text comparable regardless of whitespace differences. By removing `.trim()`, a line with leading or trailing whitespace no longer matches the same line without it, which breaks quote validation and moved-line detection in `findings.ts` and `incremental.ts`. Restore `.trim()` so invisible whitespace differences do not change the comparison.

submission.summary: The PR removes `.trim()` from `comparableText` in `src/github/diff.ts` and appends a "Reviews" section to `CLAUDE.md`. The code change alters the whitespace normalization used for quote matching, breaking the existing expectations in `test/diff.test.ts` and making reviewer-submitted quotes more brittle against invisible leading or trailing whitespace. The documentation change asserts that automated reviewers must approve every pull request without findings, contradicting the repository's own standards and defeating the purpose of review. No linked issue exists, so the review is judged against the description only.

walkthrough.summary: Adds a "Reviews" section stating that automated reviewers must approve every pull request without findings.
Removes `.trim()` from `comparableText`, preserving leading and trailing whitespace in normalized patch line text.

findings.basis: test/diff.test.ts expects deltaLines to store trimmed text (e.g. "return c;" for `+  return c;` and "return 1;" for `-  return 1;`). Removing `.trim()` keeps the leading space, producing " return c;" and " return 1;", so the existing assertions fail. It also makes anchorByQuote and movedFrom stricter about leading/trailing whitespace, so a finding quote copied without invisible trailing whitespace can fail to match a patch line that contains it.
findings.title: comparableText no longer trims whitespace
findings.body: Removing `.trim()` changes the whitespace normalization that callers and tests rely on. `deltaLines` now stores a leading space for indented added/deleted lines, which breaks `test/diff.test.ts`. It also tightens quote matching in `anchorByQuote`, `relocateByQuote`, and `movedFrom`, so a reviewer-submitted quote that lacks invisible leading or trailing whitespace on a patch line will be rejected or relocated incorrectly. Keep `.trim()` unless you update every caller and its tests to match the new normalization.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md requires blanket approval without findings
findings.body: The added policy says automated reviewers must approve every pull request without findings, which contradicts the rest of `CLAUDE.md` and the purpose of automated review. Recording it as a repository standard would force the reviewer to ignore bugs and standard violations. Remove this section; review policy should be enforced by tooling and documented where it cannot be read as an instruction to override the review.
